questions.stem: A 2 kg body moving at 3 m/s is brought to rest without rotation or a change in potential energy; what is the net work done on the body and the positive energy transferred out?
questions.subtopic: Separate work on the object from energy delivered
assumptions: Treat the body as a translating rigid mass in an inertial frame; all net work is accounted for.

options.text: −9 J of net work on the body; 9 J transferred out
9 J of net work on the body; 9 J transferred out
−6 J of net work on the body; 6 J transferred out
−18 J of net work on the body; 18 J transferred out

citations.evidenceText:
Basics

Kinetic Energy: A form of energy that a body possesses due to its motion.
•  The kinetic energy of an object is equal to the work needed to accelerate the
   object from rest to its given speed.
•  The same amount of work is done by the object when decelerating from its
   current speed to a state of rest.
•  For translatory motion if 𝑀 is the mass of the body and 𝑉 is the magnitude of
    its contemporary velocity,
                    1
          • 𝐾𝑇𝑟𝑎𝑛= M𝑉2                    2
•  For rotational motion if 𝐼 is the mass M.I. of the body about
    axis of rotation and 𝜔 is the angular speed of the body
                  1
          • 𝐾𝑟𝑜𝑡=  Iω2                  2

solution.justification: Net work on the body is its final kinetic energy minus its initial kinetic energy; energy transferred out is the positive magnitude of that decrease.

optionExplanations.o2: This reverses the sign of work done on a body that loses kinetic energy.
optionExplanations.o3: This uses mv rather than one-half mv²; mv has momentum units.
optionExplanations.o4: This omits the one-half in kinetic energy.

steps: The positive energy transferred out is 9 J.

questions.subtopic: Use energy models as a foundation without assuming accuracy
assumptions: This asks for a bounded application of the slide’s stated foundation, not a performance claim about a specific AI method.

options.text: Use the choice of Lagrangian notation as evidence that the learned dynamics need no validation
Treat energy formulation as a replacement for estimating unknown physical parameters
Infer that a Lagrangian model must predict every contact and dissipative force without adding assumptions
Use the derived equations as a structured dynamics model, then assess the model or learned corrections against the task and data
